clue.text: A county council ring road grant?

parts.note: CC is the standard abbreviation for county council
a ring is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: A local authority considering funding for a ring road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grant' looks like a noun for money; here it is the verb, to give or concede.
explanation.definitionFit: To accord someone something is to give or allow it to them, a synonym of granting.

clue.text: Make it known the girl's gained little weight

parts.note: an ounce is a small unit of weight

explanation.surface: Telling everyone that a young woman has put on a bit of weight.
explanation.definitionFit: To declare something publicly is to make it known.

indicators.note: the letters given are assembled into a new structure

explanation.surface: A memorial that was costly to construct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to build' rearranges the letters of NOT CHEAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A war memorial such as the one in Whitehall is a monument to the dead.

clue.text: About to include it in the ceremony

indicators.note: the word for about takes the next word inside it

explanation.surface: A ceremony about to begin that will feature something.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal religious or solemn act is a ceremony.

explanation.surface: A kitchen scene where pressure is used to drain something.
explanation.definitionFit: Pouring through a sieve separates out the liquid; a person who is tense and stretched is also described this way.

parts.note: the court is a sports court, not a law court, and the official sits in a tall chair

explanation.surface: A judge carried shoulder-high by admirers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court official' suggests a legal clerk; 'chaired on high' sounds like being carried in triumph, but describes the tall chair at Wimbledon.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjudicator at a tennis match sits in a high chair beside the net.

explanation.surface: Someone who is out on the golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: Absent means gone off; a team playing on another side's ground is playing an away match.

indicators.note: a new form made from the letters means they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rigid, settled kind of refusal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fastened in place with nails is fixed.

explanation.surface: Someone tailed by a determined pursuer.
explanation.definitionFit: To dog someone is to follow them closely; tenacious determination is dogged persistence.

clue.text: This will appear at the end of the Eighties

definitions.text: This will appear at the end of the Eighties

parts.words: This will appear at the end of the Eighties
parts.note: counting upwards, once the numbers eighty to eighty-nine are exhausted, the next number arrives

explanation.surface: A remark about something that turned up as a decade closed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Eighties' sounds like the 1980s decade, but read it as the run of numbers from eighty to eighty-nine.
explanation.definitionFit: The number following eighty-nine closes off the run of numbers in the eighties.

explanation.surface: A report of a battle going well.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops in combat are said to be engaging the enemy; a winning manner is a charming, attractive one.

parts.note: a section is a military unit, part of a larger force such as a brigade

explanation.surface: Evidence taken from the Angry Brigade, a 1970s British militant group.
explanation.walkthrough: The Angry Brigade was a British militant group of the early 1970s, which makes the surface sound like a police inquiry.
explanation.definitionFit: A representative slice of a population is a typical sample.

explanation.surface: Someone sizing up whether a person can carry out a plot.
explanation.definitionFit: Being equal to a task means being capable of it; a person plotting mischief is said to be 'up to something'.

explanation.surface: A runner who is falling behind on the race course.
explanation.definitionFit: A team behind on the score is said to be trailing; a path through countryside is also a trail.

clue.text: Now this will get you nowhere

definitions.note: 'here and now' pairs the two words as meaning the present moment

indicators.note: the following word yields the required letters from inside it, so the end of that word provides them

explanation.surface: A warning that some course of action is futile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Now' followed by 'this' makes NOWHERE, so the answer sits in 'nowhere' after the NOW; 'Now' also defines it, as in 'here and now'.
explanation.definitionFit: At this point in time, as in 'here we go' or 'here and now', the present moment.

clue.text: University head in no panic to get to wedding

indicators.note: the head of the word is its opening letter
in a panic the letters scatter into a new order

explanation.surface: A university principal staying calm on the way to a wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' takes U from University, and 'panic' rearranges IN NO into NION.
explanation.definitionFit: A marriage is a joining of two people, so a wedding is a union.

explanation.surface: A course of study for a vocalist.
explanation.definitionFit: The general drift or direction of something is its tenor; the highest natural adult male voice is also a tenor.

parts.note: the pair is not friends at a pub but two pieces of crockery that always go together at tea time

explanation.surface: Ordinary pals who meet for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Companions' suggests people; it is two items of tableware that are always paired.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea-time pairing of crockery used every day for hot drinks.

parts.note: not someone promising to be quick, but a competitor finishing in second place

explanation.surface: Someone saying they will be back in a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only be a second' sounds like 'back in a moment'; it means finishing second.
explanation.definitionFit: The competitor placed second, just behind the winner.

indicators.note: the letters given point to the answer once rearranged

explanation.surface: A coat-of-arms crest can reveal family lineage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may indicate' rearranges ANY CREST; the whole clue also describes the answer, since a heraldic crest points to family descent.
explanation.definitionFit: A heraldic crest shows a family's lineage and descent.

parts.note: a newspaper feature reporting the doings of high society

explanation.surface: A comment on some trait of society at large.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feature' means a regular newspaper piece and 'society' the fashionable set it reports on.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper page of tittle-tattle about celebrities and the fashionable set.

explanation.surface: Capital punishment carried out in an old-fashioned way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' here is money or goods held, and the old punishment was a wooden frame holding the offender's ankles.
explanation.definitionFit: Shares and holdings make up capital; the wooden frame for holding offenders in public was a punishment.

explanation.surface: A wild cat let loose on the highways.
explanation.definitionFit: A big spotted American cat; also a British make of luxury car.

explanation.surface: A horse-drawn vehicle with springs.
explanation.definitionFit: A light two-wheeled pony carriage; also a snare that is sprung to catch an animal.

clue.text: It's worn in one's car for warmth

definitions.text: It's worn in one's car for warmth

indicators.note: the letters needed sit inside the words that follow, running across the word breaks

explanation.surface: Something a driver wears to keep warm on a cold journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to the run hidden across 'one'S CAR For'; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip of wool wound round the neck to keep the wearer warm.

indicators.note: the word Mrs is to be left out of the surname that follows

parts.note: the title gives its own three letters to be removed

explanation.surface: Distinguishing two married women by their surnames.
explanation.walkthrough: Princess Anne was married to Mark Phillips, making her Mrs Phillips. 'not' strips the letters M, R, S out of MANNERS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Princess Royal took the surname Phillips on her first marriage to Captain Mark Phillips.

explanation.surface: A detective's clue found in a chest of drawers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawer' looks like a piece of furniture; it is a person who draws, using a pencil.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointer for detectives is a clue; the graphite core of a pencil is used by an artist.

explanation.surface: Telling someone to observe a nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the nobility sitting in the House of Lords; to gaze closely is also this verb.

clue.text: Well brought up, but lacking refinement

explanation.surface: Someone raised with good manners who still lacks polish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well brought up' sounds like good upbringing; read it as pumped up from an oil well.
explanation.definitionFit: Petroleum pumped from a well before processing; untreated means unrefined.

explanation.surface: A creature on the hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: A small weasel-like mammal used for rabbiting; to search persistently is to ferret about.

clue.text: Point to missile launched from submarine grating

parts.note: S, for south, is a compass point
Trident is the submarine-launched ballistic missile used by the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Directions for firing a missile from a submarine through a grating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grating' looks like a grille on a submarine; it is the adjective meaning harsh-sounding.
explanation.definitionFit: A harsh, loud sound is grating on the ear.

clue.text: Hop around in an attempt to get a prize

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go inside the word for an attempt
the letters of the word hop are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone hopping about trying to win a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns HOP into OPH, and 'in' puts that inside TRY.
explanation.definitionFit: A cup or award given to a winner is a prize.
